changelog: fix: 2.9.3 made the update problem worse and this undoes it. That version swept backend/Rplots.pdf and frontend/package-lock.json by running `git rm --cached` on them, which leaves a STAGED DELETION in the index permanently. On the next run the file is no longer in the index, so `git ls-files --error-unmatch` fails and the sweep skips it — while the staged deletion still counts as a change and stops the update. It therefore worked exactly once per machine and then wedged that machine for good, with a message telling the user to stash build output. The original bug at least left you able to stash and continue. Two changes. update.sh now REPAIRS a machine left in that state, unstaging the leftover index entry so it recovers by itself with no manual git. And it DISCARDS the regenerated files rather than untracking them: whether a file belongs in the repo is one decision, made once, in a commit from the development machine, not something each runtime machine does to its own index behind the others' backs. The dirty check now excludes the whole regenerated list rather than only what the current run happened to touch, which is what makes it behave the same on the first run and the hundredth. Note that package-lock.json stays tracked — a lockfile belongs in the repo; the fix for that one was 2.8.6 switching to `npm ci`, which does not write it. Only Rplots.pdf needs untracking, once, upstream. Verified against a repo reproducing the wedged state: it repairs, it is repeatable across runs, and a genuine local edit still stops the update both alone and alongside machine output.
